claim_verdicts.evidence: Definition of the lesson's own vocab term, identical to track.yaml outline item 1 and the glossary entry; nothing version-dependent to source.

Program.cs @ stage-2 L75-80: comment "Redis is left out on purpose", then AddHealthChecks().AddDbContextCheck<DonHangDbContext>(tags: ["ready"]); grep for health/AddCheck finds no other check. L123-124: MapHealthChecks("/health/live", Predicate = _ => false) and "/health/ready" with Predicate = check => check.Tags.Contains("ready"). No mail-server check anywhere.

"By default: The `DbContextHealthCheck` calls EF Core's `CanConnectAsync` method. You can customize what operation is run when checking health by using `AddDbContextCheck` method overloads." (monikerRange '>= aspnetcore-3.1', ms.date 02/25/2026)

"The following StatusCodes assignments are the default values used by the middleware": [HealthStatus.Healthy] = Status200OK, [HealthStatus.Degraded] = Status200OK, [HealthStatus.Unhealthy] = Status503ServiceUnavailable. Captured outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/health.txt shows 200 OK Healthy and, for api-no-db, 503 Service Unavailable.

probes.md: "If the readiness probe returns a failed state, the EndpointSlice controller removes the Pod's IP address from the EndpointSlices of all Services that match the Pod." Restarts are tied to liveness: "Liveness probes determine when to restart a container." api.yaml @ stage-2 liveness hits /health/live, which runs no check.

ProductCache.cs @ stage-2 L71 `catch (Exception ex) when (ex is RedisException or RedisTimeoutException)`, L73 logger.LogWarning(...), L74 `return null;`. No other catch in GetAsync, so other exceptions propagate.

L28-29 GetAsync; null -> under the per-key lock GetAsync again (L38-39), then L41 `inner.FindAsync(id); // cache miss: one query`. ProductsController @ stage-2: only single-product reads go through IProductRepository. Round 3: s5 now omits the second Redis try ("FindAsync ... treats as a miss: it calls inner.FindAsync, one PostgreSQL query"); still true, since with Redis down the second try also returns null.

Claim narrowed to repo facts (round 2). Round 1 git show stage-2: ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs L36 `options.BacklogPolicy = BacklogPolicy.FailFast;`, api-configmap.yaml and docker-compose.yml `ConnectionStrings__Redis: "redis:6379,abortConnect=false"`. Round 2: outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/configmap.txt L2 `ConnectionStrings__Redis=redis:6379,abortConnect=false`. No library behaviour is asserted any more, so no docs evidence is needed.

QueuedNotifier.Send @ stage-2 only calls `db.Notifications.Add(new Notification { Order = order, Channel = "email", Subject = subject, Status = "pending", CreatedAt = now, NextAttemptAt = now })`; the class takes only DonHangDbContext, no email sender.

outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/email-retry.txt: "mailpit is stopped: every send fails" / "== POST /api/v1/orders as customer 1" / "  -> 201" / attempts 1-4 "next attempt in 2/4/8/16 s" / "failed on attempt 5; giving up" / "failed | 5 | t".

NotificationSender.cs @ stage-2: `MaxAttempts = 5`; RecordFailure: `Attempts++; if (Attempts >= MaxAttempts) { Status = "failed"; ... return; }`, never picked up again. email-retry.sh: "about 40 s in all". Round 3 wording (s4 node "lost if still down after 5 attempts", summary 4 "an outage outlasting five attempts (about 40 s) loses them") matches.

api.yaml @ stage-2: `replicas: 2`, readinessProbe httpGet path /health/ready port 8080. redis.yaml: Deployment redis `replicas: 1`, Service redis port 6379. api-configmap.yaml: `ConnectionStrings__Redis: "redis:6379,abortConnect=false"` (same for every api Pod via envFrom).

Reworded s6 symptom (every request through the Service fails although PostgreSQL is up) follows from claim 12 (both api Pods use the one redis:6379) and probes.md: a failed readiness probe removes "the Pod's IP address from the EndpointSlices of all Services that match the Pod". A shared dependency in the ready check fails every Pod's probe together, leaving Service api with no endpoints.

Mechanism supported by code and run: ProductCache L41 sends every miss to inner.FindAsync, and cache-aside.txt shows the hit costs "queries PostgreSQL ran for it: 0" while the Redis-stopped read costs 1. Now limited to single-product reads (claim 7). "Safe only while PostgreSQL can carry it" is a conditional judgement, worded with its condition.

Design judgement with its condition stated ("when the empty result is a wrong answer"); the code part (ProductCache catches only Redis errors and returns the real product via PostgreSQL) is covered by claims 6-7.

cache-aside.sh @ stage-2: `redis DEL product:3`, get_product_3 twice ("cache miss", "cache hit"), then `docker compose stop redis`, get_product_3, `docker compose start redis`, `docker compose up --wait redis`. get_product_3 prints `-> %{http_code}` and "queries PostgreSQL ran for it: N" (counts 'FROM products' in api log). scripts/up.sh exists at stage-2.
cache-aside.txt: three times `{"id":3,"name":"Tai nghe","priceVnd":890000}  -> 200`; "queries PostgreSQL ran for it: 1", then "0", then ("with the redis container stopped") "1".

ProductCache.cs L18 `private static readonly TimeSpan Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);` used in SetAsync `StringSetAsync(key, json, Ttl)`; UpdatePriceAsync L56-57 saves then `RemoveAsync($"product:{id}")`.
